body_markdown:
Mycoplasma contamination is a persistent QC challenge in cell and gene therapy (CGT), where products are short‑lived, patient‑specific, and highly vulnerable to microbial disruption1,2. Because compendial culture-based tests, compliant with Ph. Eur. 2.6.7, can typically take 21–28 days for result generation, they create release bottlenecks fundamentally misaligned with the accelerated CGT timelines1,2


Mycoplasmas lack a cell wall and often evade routine microbial tests; even low‑level contamination can alter cell behavior and compromise safety and potency—risks magnified in time‑compressed CGT manufacturing windows1,2. Regulatory expectations anchor mycoplasma control within the manufacturing control strategy for cell‑derived products; FDA‑aligned perspectives emphasize testing at stages where contamination is most likely to be detected for genetically engineered cell products1


Across major pharmacopeias, nucleic acid amplification technique (NAT) methods (PCR/qPCR/dPCR) are recognized as acceptable alternatives to culture when appropriately validated for sensitivity, specificity, and robustness—e.g., Ph. Eur. 2.6.7, USP <63>, and JP harmonized chapters—supporting rapid detection compatible with CGT workflows3,4,5,6.


Labcorp’s rapid ddPCR mycoplasma testing enables highly sensitive, specific detection within hours rather than weeks, supporting real‑time or near‑real‑time batch disposition and shortening manufacturing holds while aligning with pharmacopeial validation frameworks for alternative methods (Ph. Eur. 2.6.7, USP <63>, JP) and FDA’s risk‑based expectations1,3,5,6 and is now available as part of the GMP BioPharmaceutical CMC Solutions service portfolio.


## Data/Findings


Labcorp has completed a GMP compliant validation of the BioRad VeriCheck Mycoplasma ddPCR kit to implement rapid mycoplasma testing within the BioPharmaceutical CMC Solutions services.


The full panel of mycoplasma species as outlined in EP2.6.74 were analyzed at a concentration of 10 cfu/ml through the BioRad VeriCheck Mycoplasma ddPCR kit. The data outlined in Figure 1 confirm that all pharmacopeial mycoplasma species are detected within the required limit of detection (LOD) of 10 cfu/mL


In addition, specificity controls of closely related bacterial species were also analyzed in accordance with EP2.6.7 as part of method development, as well as three typically used cell lines used in CGT manufacturing (CHO, HEK and Vero Cell lines). As confirmed in figure 1, these samples were negative for the presence of mycoplasma, supporting assay specificity and suitability for CGT manufacturing matrices.

Figure 1 details the copies/µL mycoplasma detected for each tested mycoplasma species and associated specificity controls. The positive cut off refers to the result at which a sample is determined positive for mycoplasma (>0.1copies/µL)


## Conclusion


Mycoplasma contamination remains a significant risk in cell and gene therapy manufacturing, where prolonged culture‑based testing timelines are incompatible with accelerated, patient‑specific production models. Rapid nucleic acid amplification–based testing offers a viable alternative to overcome these constraints, and the data presented here support the implementation of Labcorp’s newly validated ddPCR‑based mycoplasma assay as part of its GMP BioPharmaceutical CMC Solutions service offering. This method demonstrates sensitive and specific detection across the full pharmacopeial mycoplasma panel at the required LOD, while reducing time‑to‑result from weeks to hours in alignment with Ph. Eur. 2.6.7, USP <63> and other harmonized regulatory frameworks. Through this new offering, Labcorp enables near‑real‑time batch disposition and strengthened microbial control strategies, ultimately supporting more agile manufacturing and the timely delivery of safe, high‑quality therapies to patients.
